system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

exchanges.user:
ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
**Buyer-side review — Wattlebridge Holdings.** The positions below are proposed negotiating asks, not agreed terms. The underlying DD documents and full SPA have not been provided, so factual conclusions remain subject to verification.

| Issue | Seller’s position | What the Buyer should want | Recommendation and one-line reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001 — General liability cap** | General warranty liability capped at **20% / AUD 4.8m**. | A materially higher general cap, without absorbing separate claim categories. | **Counter at 100% / AUD 24m**, with any reduction commercially negotiated; a 20% cap leaves substantial acquisition risk with Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-002 — De minimis & basket** | Claims must exceed **AUD 25,000**; **AUD 250,000 deductible basket**, recovering only the excess. | Lower thresholds, a tipping basket and aggregation of related claims. | **Propose AUD 10,000 de minimis and AUD 100,000 tipping basket**, restricted to general warranties; Seller’s combination materially erodes recovery. |
| **SPA-N-003 — General claims time limit** | Notification within **18 months**; limitations extend to all Claims unless expressly excluded. | At least two full reporting cycles and category-specific survival periods. | **Seek 36 months for general warranties**, with reasonable notice requirements and no short proceedings deadline; 18 months may expire before latent issues emerge. |
| **SPA-N-004 — Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title share general warranty caps and deadlines. | Separate protection for ownership, capacity, authority and unencumbered transfer, without thresholds. | **Require a separate 100%-of-price cap and survival through the applicable statutory limitation period**; Buyer must retain meaningful recourse if Seller cannot deliver the shares promised. |
| **SPA-N-005 — Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to all Claims; no express fraud exception is supplied. | An overriding carve-out for fraud, fraudulent misrepresentation and fraudulent concealment attributable to Seller, preserving non-excludable rights. | **Expressly disapply contractual caps, thresholds, time bars and remedy/reliance restrictions to those claims**; Seller must not obtain contractual protection for its own fraud. |
| **SPA-N-006 — Disclosure scope** | Blanket disclosure of the data room, referenced materials, accounts, registers and public records. | Only matters fairly disclosed with sufficient detail to identify their nature and scope, against relevant warranties. | **Reject blanket disclosure; agree a frozen, indexed disclosure bundle and specific disclosures**, without automatic qualification of title warranties or indemnities; document availability is not meaningful disclosure. |
| **SPA-N-007 — Buyer knowledge qualifier** | Bars claims for Buyer/adviser knowledge, including matters merely discoverable. | No knowledge exclusion; alternatively, narrowly defined actual knowledge of named Buyer personnel. | **Delete constructive, imputed and adviser knowledge**, with Seller bearing proof of any agreed actual-knowledge defence; diligence should not transfer undiscovered risks to Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-008 — Bluefen consent** | Reasonable endeavours; condition satisfied by delivery of written consent, although final consent and satisfaction of associated conditions are absent. | A substantive completion condition covering clause 11.2 consent **and clause 11.3 conditions**, without unacceptable commercial changes. | **Require effective consent and evidence that associated conditions are satisfied before Completion, waivable only by Buyer**; approximately 30% of revenue is exposed. |
| **SPA-N-009 — Riverlark facility** | Approximately **AUD 3.2m** outstanding; security release follows Completion. | Repayment and effective release of all relevant security at Completion under a binding payoff arrangement. | **Require a verified payout letter, direct repayment through funds flow and simultaneous effective releases**, with subsequent registration filings controlled; Buyer should not acquire a still-secured business on a promise of later release. |
| **SPA-N-010 — Employee bonuses** | **AUD 420,000** conditional bonuses are described as Seller’s responsibility but omitted from funds flow; on-costs unspecified. | Seller-funded treatment of all qualifying bonuses and applicable payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs. | **Expressly allocate liability, quantify on-costs and include payment or a price adjustment plus indemnity, without double counting**; an allocation unsupported by completion mechanics leaves Buyer funding the obligation. |
| **SPA-N-011 — Ironquay IP indemnity** | Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; AUD 180,000 is recorded open, but non-payment is not independently verified and no assignment is supplied. | Verified payment status and a complete, effective IP transfer, plus protection against resulting ownership and use risks. | **Require payment verification and confirmatory assignment before Completion; broaden the indemnity beyond the fee to resulting losses and remediation costs**, outside general thresholds; paying an invoice alone may not resolve the IP risk. |
| **SPA-N-012 — Export/privacy incident** | Preliminary operational matter, said unlikely to be material; access, scope and notification requirements remain unresolved. | Prompt investigation, evidence preservation, legally required notifications and remediation, backed by specific risk allocation. | **Require an investigation/update covenant and a specific indemnity for the pre-Completion incident, with proportionate completion protection if findings are material**; neither a confirmed notifiable breach nor immateriality is established. |
| **SPA-N-013 — Sandbar renewals** | Three **AUD 110,000** renewals, **AUD 330,000 aggregate**, characterised as ordinary-course costs. | Assessment of the connected commitments together, including timing, cancellation rights, accrual and benefit period. | **Review DD-008 and DD-011 together and restrict unapproved commitments pending Completion; adjust price only where the agreed accounting treatment supports it**; neither ordinary-course status nor automatic debt treatment is established. |
| **SPA-N-014 — Category separation** | Broad limitations and remedy restrictions apply across all Claims unless expressly excepted. | Distinct regimes for general warranties, fundamentals, tax, specific indemnities, fraud and payment/completion obligations. | **Insert an express category matrix and precedence clause**, excluding special categories from general limitations unless specifically agreed; blanket drafting could defeat separately negotiated protections. |
| **SPA-N-015 — Title verification** | Relies on DD-012’s register showing Seller holds 100% of issued shares. | Independent confirmation of the entire capital structure, Seller’s ownership and absence of encumbrances or competing rights. | **Check the register against corporate records, issuance/transfer documents, certificates and relevant security searches; require clear-title warranties and completion deliverables**; a register entry alone does not establish unencumbered title. |
| **SPA-N-016 — Tax/IP open terms** | Tax and IP warranties treated as settled within the general regime. | A separate pre-Completion tax indemnity and appropriate tax warranties; robust IP ownership, licensing and infringement protection beyond Ironquay. | **Reopen both: seek tax survival of at least seven years, extended for live assessments, and longer IP survival with separately negotiated caps**; neither category is adequately addressed by an 18-month, 20% general regime. |

**Drafting discipline:** Carry every agreed exception through clauses **9.3, 12, 13 and 20.5**, the disclosure provisions and all relevant definitions—not merely the individual warranty or indemnity.
=== END ADVICE ===
